LESSON: DIVISION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.3: Division
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Division, part of Numbers in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you estimate quotients? 2. How is division used in real life? 3. How can you work out questions involving combined operations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the steps involved in divide up to a 4-digit number by up to a 3-digit number where the dividend is greater than the divisor in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Division in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. divide up to a 4-digit number by up to a 3- digit number where the dividend is greater than the divisor in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Division in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. estimate quotients by rounding off the dividend and divisor to the nearest ten in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Division in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Division together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner develops speaking skills and teamwork as they discuss on the relationship

between multiplication and division.

Values:
• Respect: The learner values each other’s opinion when dividing up to a 4-digit number by up to a 3-digit number and share

answers in class.

PCIs:

• Safety and security: The learner observes internet safety and security by accessing safe online mathematical sites to play

digital games on division of whole numbers.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• English and other Languages: The learner reinforces speaking and listening skills during discussion on the relationship

between multiplication and division.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Cubes and cubarithm board, abacus, Taylor frames with plastic types, number board, talking calculator, Braille charts, charts

and cards with appropriate font and colour contrast, reference material in braille and in appropriate print
